Vita JP Overlay

Learn Japanese with your PS Vita for free

Look up words from the games you play, entirely offline

Text recognition and the dictionary run on the Vita itself

Create flashcards of words you don't know

With card mining on, × saves the word to a queue on the memory card

Export them as Lapis cards for Anki

with the word, its reading, the sentence and the definition

Export cards to a dated .apkg file

Import it into Anki on any device

It only runs in the games you turn on

and reads new text once, after it settles on screen

Easy install

plus a one-time setup: a script on your computer over VitaShell's FTP, the app in VitaShell, a reboot

Now it's installed: go to your game and press L + R to look up words.

Turn it off for specific games, so it doesn't get in the way

The Overlay app opens beside your game, which stays suspended

Card queue 23 cards · works offline

If it fails to boot at all, hold L while powering on and run: tools/install_ftp.sh --uninstall 192.168.1.42​+----------------------------------------------------------------------------+| ONE MORE STEP: install the Overlay app (JPOverlaySettings.vpk) || || No Overlay app is installed on the Vita (ux0:app/VJOSET001). || || Do it now, before you reboot: in VitaShell, press OK on the FTP dialog to || keep FTP running, open ux0:data/, select JPOverlaySettings.vpk, press the || confirm button (x on most consoles, o on Japanese ones) and confirm the || install. || || Then check it from here, with VitaShell's FTP still running: bash || install-vita.sh --check-app 192.168.1.42, then reboot. || || An older app shows engines and pages that are gone and saves settings the || plugins no longer use (test.2's run had test.1's app writing ocr_backend = || vocr2, #101). |+----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
1VitaShell: set SELECT button to FTP (once)
2Run install-vita.sh on your computer
3Install the Overlay app in VitaShell
4Reboot
